I will start from what worked the last 4 years here in Quzhou and then adjust by field condition, water, and crop value. I farm 225 mu, so I have to think in terms of total output and cash flow, not just one plot at a time. I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is still my stable base with well irrigation, and I will keep a smaller block in cotton for cash income and to spread risk. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard, because if wheat or maize loses yield, that loss is bigger than saving a few bags of input. But I also do not want blind overuse, so I will set rates around realistic yield targets for our area: wheat around 550 kg per mu, summer maize around 650 kg per mu, and cotton around 320 kg per mu. For wheat I will hold nitrogen a bit higher because it responds well with irrigation; for maize I will keep strong nitrogen and enough potassium so the stalk stays strong after wheat; for cotton I will not chase very high nitrogen because too much vegetative growth gives me trouble later. On tillage, I will use rotary or plough where I need better seedbed, and for summer maize after wheat I will go no-tillage to save time and catch moisture. I will spray based on the problems I usually see here, and because I have water from wells, I will not let the key growth stages go dry.
